key_insight: The paper extends the classic mixing-plane interface to compressible reacting-mixture flows by enforcing a thermodynamically consistent mixed-out state through nested pressure and enthalpy solves.
engineering_relevance: This enables steady whole-engine turbomachinery simulations that couple compressor, combustor, and turbine without losing conservation or physical consistency across composition-changing interfaces.
method: Outer search for the interface pressure root.
Inner enthalpy inversion to recover the mixed thermodynamic state.
Physical-state checks plus power-law pressure sampling for robustness near low normal velocity.
evidence_signal: Validated on a quasi-1D interface test, a Darmstadt transonic compressor case, and a KJ66 micro-turbojet whole-engine simulation, with maximum relative mass-flow error below 0.11% across mixing planes.
watch_item: The nested nonlinear solve can become stiff near low normal velocities, so robust root-bracketing and state validation are important in implementation.
paper_title: Generalised Mixing-Plane Method for Compressible Reacting-Mixture Flows in Steady Multiphysics Turbomachinery Simulations
